clue.text: Liquid refreshment?

parts.note: not a drink at all: the refreshment is a treatment of the body by means of water

explanation.surface: Seems to offer someone a drink after a long day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid refreshment' normally means a drink; here it is a restorative therapy that uses water, such as baths or exercises in a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrotherapy is medical treatment using water, a refreshing cure delivered through a liquid.

clue.text: Rash man to sup oddly in time

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

indicators.note: oddly signals the letters of to sup are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: An impetuous man drinks strangely at the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' scrambles to sup into OTSPU. Hotspur was the nickname of Sir Henry Percy, the hot-headed rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a rash, hot-headed person, named after Harry Percy in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Diction rather associated with languor, principally

definitions.text: Diction rather associated with languor, principally

indicators.note: principally means taking the principal, leading, letter of each word

explanation.surface: Describes a lazy way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lazy manner of speech, linked with languor.

clue.text: Some buffoons laugh, taking charge

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Clowns laugh as they take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack, as is a charge by troops.

clue.text: Note that man would put around base

indicators.note: put around means the first piece is placed round the second

parts.note: he'd is short for he would, that man would
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A man leaves a note around his base.
explanation.walkthrough: HE'D surrounds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to take notice of it, to heed it.

clue.text: Turn to revolutionary, in part

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a ration is a portion, a part allotted

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over, so the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone turns to revolution, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like politics but just means turned round, giving OT; 'Turn' is the definition, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotation is a turn, one revolution or a taking of turns in sequence.

clue.text: Student is finished, caught by rising impudence

indicators.note: caught by means the second piece is held inside the first
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, impudence
up means finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A student is done for, caught being cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' makes PIL in this down clue; 'is finished' is a phrase giving UP, as in 'time is up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is someone being taught, a student at school.

clue.text: Street people wearing check robe

indicators.note: wearing means the first piece is clothed by the second, so goes inside it

parts.note: to vet is to check
men are people

explanation.surface: People on the street wearing a checked robe.
explanation.walkthrough: STMEN goes inside VET.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial garment, such as a priest's robe.

clue.text: Disturbs, making a racket in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a racket is a noise

explanation.surface: Someone is disturbed by a loud racket during a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: A NOISE said out loud sounds like ANNOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy is to irritate or bother, which is to disturb someone.

clue.text: New skill backing broadcast traps one fugitive

indicators.note: backing means the words for new and skill are read backwards, last letter first

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: traps means one piece closes round the other and holds it inside

parts.note: sent, as in sent out over the airwaves, means broadcast
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone escapes by broadcasting their new trapping skills in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NART into TRAN; 'traps' puts I inside SENT to make SIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugitive as an adjective means fleeting or passing, the same sense as transient.

clue.text: Groom and page never returned

indicators.note: returned means the poetic form of never is read backwards

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: A groom and a page boy who never came back from the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NEER into REEN; 'Groom' is a verb here, not the bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to tidy one's appearance carefully, which is to groom oneself.

clue.text: Support rent about everybody rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the whole assembly is sent back, read from end to start
about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: a rip is a rent, a tear in fabric
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Rent support is refused for everybody in the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not money paid but a tear; 'rejected' reverses the whole assembly, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is a column that holds up a structure, a physical support.

clue.text: Knife given excessive turning by upright member

parts.note: a stile is a vertical piece in the frame of a door or window

indicators.note: turning means the abbreviation for excessive is read backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A knife is twisted to excess by an upstanding member of the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes TTO of OTT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slender dagger with a narrow pointed blade, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Reject wasting second for grand asylum

indicators.note: wasting second for grand means the S is thrown away and G put in its place

parts.note: to refuse something is to reject it
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An asylum seeker is rejected, losing a second chance at a grand fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting second for grand' swaps the S of REFUSE for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum means shelter or sanctuary, and a refuge is a place of safety.

clue.text: Love god overly feminine turning tender

indicators.note: turning means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
too means overly, excessively

explanation.surface: The god of love turns tender, overly feminine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses EROSTOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet that are tender and sore from walking are footsore.

clue.text: Crush hearts admitting politician succeeded

indicators.note: admitting means the first word lets the second in

parts.note: cores are hearts, the centres of things
MP, a Member of Parliament, is a politician
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A politician won the hearts of a crush and succeeded.
explanation.walkthrough: S for succeeded comes from family trees, where it marks who succeeded whom.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress is to squeeze or press together, which is to crush.

clue.text: Avoid endless beer during that pandemic

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to prevent something is to avoid it happening

indicators.note: endless means the word for beer loses its last letter

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: Avoid endless drinking during the pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims beer to AL. 'pandemic' is used as an adjective, widespread, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandemic as an adjective means widespread over a whole area, so widely prevalent.

clue.text: Cigarettes in abundance holding drink up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
holding means the phrase contains the letters within it

explanation.surface: Plenty of cigarettes and drink being held up.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ETTESINA sits inside the words; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet liqueur flavoured with aniseed, a drink.

clue.text: Blasting last of birds making owl noises

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of birds

parts.note: hooting is the noise owls make

explanation.surface: Birds are being blasted while owls hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting means firing guns, blasting away at a target.

clue.text: It's finally his own razor, initially

definitions.note: It's means it is, the thing referred to; the 's acts as a link

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of his

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of razor

explanation.surface: A young man finally gets a razor of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the definition: the whole clue reads as a description of the thing, an electric razor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaver is an electric razor, the object pointed to by the pronoun as a cryptic reference.

clue.text: Let rapture not end all empty

indicators.note: all empty means every one of these words loses its inside, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Let rapture last forever, with nothing empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that has been let has been leased out to a tenant, the past participle of rent.

clue.text: Cut record time, cut by someone gutted

indicators.note: cut by means one piece is split open by the other going inside

parts.note: a disc is a record

indicators.note: gutted means the word loses its insides, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A record time was cut by someone who was devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like an emotion but means the word's inside is removed, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to cut open and take apart, as in a biology lab.

clue.text: Sailor's right circling sea's opening deep

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; with the 's it is ABS

indicators.note: circling means the word goes round the letter

parts.note: true means right, correct

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of sea's

explanation.surface: A sailor rightly circles the start of the deep sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts S inside TRUE to make TRUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep in the sense of profound or hard to understand matches abstruse, obscure.

clue.text: Occasionally great fellow produces gas

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of great

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Every so often a great fellow makes gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Worries surrounding start of incisor decay

indicators.note: surrounding means the word goes round the letter

parts.note: cares are worries

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of incisor

explanation.surface: Worries about the onset of decay in a front tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts I inside CARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical term for tooth decay, the rot in teeth or bone.

clue.text: Picture that is in publication? No

indicators.note: the question 'in publication?' is answered No: the containment runs the other way, publication inside

parts.note: mag, short for magazine, is a publication

explanation.surface: Asks whether a picture appears in a magazine; the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: The question proposes the wrong container order; 'No' says the reverse is true, so the publication sits within 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture, a likeness or representation.

clue.text: He leads among Islamic men at mosque

definitions.text: He leads among Islamic men at mosque

indicators.note: leads means taking the leading letter of each word

explanation.surface: Describes the man who leads prayers in a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads prayers among Muslims at a mosque.

clue.text: Blundered being picked up in East End

indicators.note: East End speech, Cockney, drops the H, so the word is said without it

parts.note: picked up means heard, as a sound is picked up by the ear

explanation.surface: Someone made a mistake by being caught out in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the accent of London's East End, drops initial H, so HEARD comes out as 'EARD, which sounds like ERRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so erred means made a blunder.

clue.text: Persuade European assuming period is fair

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: to tempt is to persuade or entice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Persuading a European that the period's weather is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is mild, and temperate means mild, without extremes.

clue.text: Keen to keep word 'sex' occasional

indicators.note: to keep means the first word holds the others inside

parts.note: intent means keen, eager
a term is a word
it is a common slang word for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to keep their occasional sex lives quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts TERMIT inside INTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermittent means stopping and starting at intervals, the same as occasional.
